first_record.diagnostic_basis: 1. Progressive painless vision loss in right eye for 2 years. History of phacoemulsification with IOL implantation, left eye, performed at this institution 2 years ago. History of essential hypertension for >10 years, currently self-administering Valsartan (Diovan) PO.
first_record.differential_diagnosis: (1) Traumatic cataract: Requires history of ocular trauma, often with corneal/scleral laceration; inconsistent with this patient. (2) Complicated cataract: Typically associated with systemic conditions (diabetes mellitus) or ocular inflammation (uveitis, glaucoma); lens opacities often petaloid or localized; inconsistent with this patient.
first_record.plan: 1. Complete preoperative workup; initiate topical antibiotic prophylaxis; prepare conjunctival sac. 2. Senior ophthalmologist consultation; schedule elective surgery.

other_records.record_content: Surgical indication: Diagnosis confirmed; systemic condition adequate for surgical tolerance. Procedure: Phacoemulsification with IOL implantation, right eye. Anesthesia: Local anesthesia. Precautions: Surgical necessity, potential intraoperative complications, and postoperative risks explained to patient and family; informed consent obtained and signed.

Patient underwent phacoemulsification with IOL implantation, right eye, under local anesthesia this morning. Surgical procedure: Patient positioned supine; standard sterile prep and draping; lid speculum placement; topical proparacaine anesthesia; conjunctival sac irrigation with normal saline. Clear corneal incision at 11 o'clock position, 3.0 mm width; side-port incision at 3 o'clock with keratome. 'Soft-shell technique' applied: Viscoat injected into anterior chamber followed by sodium hyaluronate to coat corneal endothelium; continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis performed with capsulorhexis forceps. Hydrodissection of cortex from capsule. Direct chop phacoemulsification technique used for nuclear fragmentation and aspiration. Residual cortex removed with I/A system. Sodium hyaluronate injected into anterior chamber and capsular bag. Foldable IOL implanted into capsular bag and centered. Viscoelastic material aspirated from anterior chamber and capsular bag. Wound hydrated to achieve self-sealing closure; IOP confirmed normal. Tobramycin/dexamethasone ointment applied to conjunctival sac; eye patched; patient returned to ward in stable condition. Postoperative care: Routine ophthalmic postoperative nursing, daily dressing changes, close monitoring.

ward_records.content: Patient in good general condition. Laboratory studies reveal no surgical contraindications. Ophthalmic examination: VA: OD 0.5, OS 0.8, -1.50 DS = 1.0. IOP: OD 13 mmHg, OS 15 mmHg. Eyelids: No edema or erythema bilaterally; lacrimal irrigation patent. OD: Conjunctiva quiet, cornea clear, AC medium depth with clear aqueous, iris with normal architecture, pupil round 3 mm with (+) light reflex, lens with grayish-white uneven opacification, fundus: optic disc with normal color and margins, retina without hemorrhage or exudate, macula with pigmentary mottling. OS: Cornea clear, AC medium depth with clear aqueous, iris normal, pupil round 3 mm with (+) light reflex, IOL well-centered in capsular bag, fundus: optic disc normal, retina without hemorrhage/exudate, macula with pigmentary mottling. Bilateral macular OCT: No significant abnormalities. Chief physician ward round: Diagnosis and treatment plan confirmed; instructed to complete preoperative workup and prepare for phacoemulsification with IOL implantation, right eye.

Patient: 76-year-old male, admitted for 'progressive painless vision loss in right eye for 2 years'. PMH: Phacoemulsification with IOL implantation, left eye, at this institution 2 years ago; essential hypertension >10 years, currently self-administering Valsartan (Diovan) PO. Admission vitals: BP 173/93 mmHg. Alert, oriented, in no acute distress. Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally; HR 70 bpm, regular rhythm, normal heart sounds, no murmurs. Ophthalmic exam: VA: OD 0.5, OS 0.8, -1.50 DS = 1.0. IOP: OD 13 mmHg, OS 15 mmHg. Eyelids: No edema/erythema; lacrimal irrigation patent. OD: Conjunctiva quiet, cornea clear, AC medium depth, aqueous clear, iris normal architecture, pupil round 3 mm with (+) light reflex, lens with grayish-white uneven opacification, fundus: optic disc normal color/margins, retina without hemorrhage/exudate, macula with pigmentary mottling and hard drusen. OS: Cornea clear, AC medium depth, aqueous clear, iris normal, pupil round 3 mm with (+) light reflex, IOL well-centered, fundus: optic disc normal, retina without hemorrhage/exudate, macula with pigmentary mottling and hard drusen. Bilateral macular OCT: No significant abnormalities. Preoperative diagnoses: 1. Cataract, right eye; 2. Pseudophakia, left eye; 3. Refractive error, bilateral; 4. Macular degeneration, bilateral; 5. Vitreous opacity, bilateral; 6. Essential hypertension.

Postoperative day 1: Patient in good general condition, denies ocular pain or headache. Ophthalmic exam: VA: OD 0.8, OS 0.8. IOP: OD 12 mmHg, OS 13 mmHg. OD: Conjunctiva quiet, cornea clear, AC medium depth with (+) aqueous flare (expected postoperative inflammatory response), iris normal architecture, pupil round 3 mm with (+) light reflex, IOL well-centered in capsular bag, fundus: optic disc normal color/margins, macula with hard exudates. OS exam unchanged from admission. Chief physician ward round: Continue topical antibiotics and steroids; daily dressing changes; close monitoring.

Postoperative day 2: Patient in good general condition, denies ocular pain or headache. Ophthalmic exam: VA: OD 0.8, OS 0.8. IOP: OD 12 mmHg, OS 12 mmHg. OD: Conjunctiva quiet, cornea clear, AC medium depth with (+) aqueous flare, iris normal, pupil round 3 mm with (+) light reflex, IOL well-centered, fundus: optic disc normal, macula with hard exudates. OS exam unchanged from admission. Chief physician ward round: Continue topical antibiotics and steroids; ophthalmic condition stable; patient cleared for discharge.

Presented to outpatient clinic today; admitted with diagnosis of 'cataract'. Since symptom onset: mental status good, appetite good, sleep good, bowel/bladder function normal.
